title: Attention runtime orchestration: prefill throttler and kernel orchestration shim
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Background: Over the last two sprints we've onboarded FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants for several LLM families. While peak throughput improved for steady-state workloads, we observed intermittent latency regressions and increased tail at prefill startup, especially for mixed sequence-length traffic and during cold-scale events. These regressions appear correlated with the current monolithic kernel selection path that picks a single kernel per-request at arrival time and with aggressive concurrent prefill bursts during bursty traffic patterns.

Problem statement: For certain model+seq length distributions, the runtime selects FlashAttention v3 kernels which perform best for long sequences but allocate larger temporary memory and have longer warmup. When a prefill burst contains a mix of short and long sequences, the v3 selection causes buffer pressure and scheduling variance, which cascades into higher tail latency and higher OOM backoffs. Our current fallback strategy is reactive (on OOM or obvious latency breach) and causes client-visible retries and degraded SLAs.

Hypothesis: Introducing a light-weight orchestration shim that decouples kernel selection from arrival-time decisions and a "prefill throttler" that paces concurrent prefill work will reduce tail latency and regressions without lowering average throughput. The shim will score kernel candidates using a compact heuristic (kp_score) that considers model, inferred sequence-length quantile, current memory headroom, and recent kernel latency samples, then apply affinity hints and delayed binding for ambiguous cases. The prefill throttler will use short-lived tokens and a startup heartbeat to stagger prefill concurrency per-GPU to reduce bursts that trigger worst-case kernel decisions.

Approach:
- Implement a Kernel Orchestration Shim (KOS) in the serving runtime: a ~400 LOC C++/Rust component that exposes a deterministic scoring function (kp_score) and an API for delayed-binding (bind-within-ms). KOS will consult model metadata and lightweight runtime telemetry.
- Implement Prefill Throttler: token-bucket based controller per-GPU that limits the number of concurrent prefill tasks and issues a startup heartbeat that spaces the first N prefill binds over a configurable window (default 50ms).
- Integrate with FlashAttention v2/v3 selector: prefer narrower-kernel when kp_score delta < threshold, and enable delayed binding for requests with high ambiguity. Provide a per-model override map for safelisting cases where v3 is always preferred.
- Add metrics and dashboards: kp_score histogram, throttler queue length, bind latency, kernel choice distribution, per-GPU prefill concurrency, OOM/backoff rate.
- E2E test plan: synthetic mixed-seq workload (short/long ratio sweeps), scale tests under autoscaling churn, regression test suite to run nightly against a canary cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
- 99th percentile prefill latency reduced by >=25% on mixed-seq synthetic workload compared to baseline (no KOS/throttler).
- OOM/backoff events during bursty prefill reduced by >=60% in canary.
- No more than 5% throughput regression at steady-state for throughput-optimized models.
- Observability: all new metrics emit and appear in the console dashboards and perf alerts created.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (prefill_throttler_v1 + kos_experiment).
2) Smoke test in staging with small-scale cluster.
3) Canary rollout to 10% of traffic for a single cpu-bound GPU pool, monitor KPIs for 48h.
4) Gradually widen to Dedicated pools with manual checkpoints.
5) Full rollout if acceptance criteria met; immediate rollback flag if 99th latency regresses >10% for more than 30min.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect kp_score tuning could bias kernel choices and reduce throughput. Mitigation: per-model safelists and canary tuning with AB tests.
- Throttling might increase client queuing latency for latency-sensitive short-seq workloads. Mitigation: exempt routes marked with low_queue_latency label and implement per-route top-up tokens.
- Complexity in runtime increases surface area for bugs. Mitigation: keep KOS small, add unit tests and fuzz the scoring function inputs.

Dependencies: "ENG-42104", "ENG-95123" (for prefilling warmup telemetry), and a design doc in Drive (link in comments).
